transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, thank you for coming back into the room. I wanted to sit down with you and talk about how things have progressed since you arrived.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay? You look very serious.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling a bit anxious. I want to be honest with you. Things didn't go quite right with how we handled your initial tests.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? Was there a mistake in the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the timing of when we looked at your heart tracing. It took a little longer than it should have to get the results reviewed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Longer? How much longer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You are the doctor. If the machine says something is wrong, you see it immediately, yes?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: In a perfect world, yes. But the system can be very overwhelming, and the notification didn't get the attention it needed right away.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt the pain in my chest. I told the nurse. I thought you were checking it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's difficult to hear that the process wasn't seamless. I can see how unsettling this is for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I trust you. I just... I thought the hospital was the safest place. If you missed something, what else did you miss?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very heavy feeling to realize there was a delay. I'm sitting here with you because I want to make sure we move forward correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen? Did you forget me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The ward was incredibly busy, and the flag on the computer screen was missed during the shift change. It happens sometimes when the volume of patients is so high.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just a patient to you. A number.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling dismissed right now. I want you to know that I am here now, and you have my full attention.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is my heart okay now? Since the delay, is there more damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a very clear path forward now. We have adjusted your medications, and we are going to do another ECG tomorrow morning at 8 AM to compare the two.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? Not now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning is the best time to see the trend. I want you to keep a log of any chest tightness you feel tonight. If you feel anything at all, even a small pressure, press the call button immediately and tell the nurse it is for the doctor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will do that. I just... I cannot believe the doctor did not see the result.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a bit of a complicated process with the digital alerts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It does not seem complicated to me. It seems like a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is distressing. It is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what to say. I expected you to have the answers.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that you look to me for leadership in your care. That makes this conversation even harder.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this happen again? With the new medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, because we have a different protocol for these specific meds. I have personally set a reminder in my phone and on the ward chart to review your stats every four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will check it yourself?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will. I'll be the one reviewing the reports personally until you are discharged.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope that is enough.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'm going to give you some time to process this. I will be back in twenty minutes to check your vitals. Please write down any questions that come to you in the meantime.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated during pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') without explicitly naming the error as a failure to review a critical test result.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'overwhelming' system and 'busy' ward.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('anxious', 'unsettling', 'dismissed') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan includes specific steps (ECG tomorrow at 8 AM), a patient role (keep a log/press call button), and a prevention strategy (personal reminders/4-hour reviews).
